label: Dual Connections
notes: Open the chapter. We now formalize the duality glimpsed in Chapter 02. The deck follows printed pages 51 through 80 and develops dual affine connections, the dually flat manifolds they define, the canonical divergence that measures separation, and the generalized Pythagorean theorem that turns the geometry into a working inference tool.

label: Dual Connections
notes: Define a pair of connections that are dual with respect to the metric: parallel transport by one preserves inner products when paired with transport by the other. The Levi-Civita connection is the average of the two. This relaxation of metric compatibility is exactly what statistical geometry requires, since estimation prefers flat affine structure to metric geodesics.

label: Dually Flat Manifolds
notes: Introduce dually flat manifolds, where one connection is flat in the e-coordinates and its dual is flat in the m-coordinates simultaneously. Exponential families realize this structure exactly. Dual flatness gives two complementary affine pictures of the same model, and it is the geometric backbone for the divergence and projection theorems that follow.

label: Canonical Divergence
notes: Define the canonical divergence from the pair of potentials through the Bregman construction. For exponential families this divergence is precisely the Kullback-Leibler divergence. It is generally asymmetric and non-metric, yet it measures separation between distributions and underlies maximum-likelihood estimation, model fitting, and the projection results of this chapter.

label: Generalized Pythagorean Theorem
notes: State the generalized Pythagorean theorem: when an e-geodesic and an m-geodesic meet orthogonally, the canonical divergences add just as squared lengths do in Euclidean space. This decomposition makes information projection well-defined and gives clean, geometric proofs of optimality for estimators and for fitting a model to data.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Dual connections relax metric compatibility, dually flat manifolds carry two complementary flat charts, the canonical divergence generalizes Kullback-Leibler, and the Pythagorean theorem decomposes it along orthogonal geodesics. This machinery powers the statistical inference developed geometrically in Chapter 04.
